No, that is not true. In Switzerland, the standard retirement age for women is 64, but this only applies to women born on or after July 1, 1960. Women born before this date retire at the older standard age of 65.

The retirement age for women is gradually being adjusted to align with that of men (65) as part of pension reform (the "AVS 21" reform), but it is not yet uniform across all women, and it will not be until the transition period is complete.
